display_name: ESA OPS-SAT (2021) — SEU Memory Corruption & Payload Safe-Mode
source_citation: ESA ESOC / Kelvins: In-Flight Operations of OPS-SAT — Anomaly & SEU Recovery (2021)
narrative_summary: In May 2021, ESA's OPS-SAT 3U CubeSat flying laboratory experienced a Single Event Upset (SEU) in the processing platform's optical payload DMA memory controller. The unhandled buffer stall triggered an OBC driver timeout loop and autonomous payload power isolation into safe-mode.

events.description: High-energy particle radiation induces SEU bit-flip in optical camera DMA controller
events.notes: Documented in ESA ESOC anomaly logs during South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) transit.

events.description: High-rate optical camera frame acquisition stalls and enters unhandled fault state
events.notes: Camera subsystem ceased transmitting image frames across SPI/AXI interface.

events.description: OBC Linux kernel payload driver thread timeout and retry storm
events.notes: OBC processing platform logged high CPU utilization handling camera interface timeouts.

events.description: Autonomous FDIR commands payload power rail shutdown to protect instrument
events.notes: EPS power distribution switch isolated payload power channel.

events.description: S-Band ground station downlink transmits spacecraft health beacon confirming payload safe-mode
events.notes: ESA ESOC ground station received nominal health beacon confirming spacecraft safe-mode isolation.
